summary: This note describes the origins of General Electric in 1889, when Thomas Edison's various electricity-related businesses were consolidated. Drexel, Morgan & Co. financed Edison's research and helped merge several Edison companies into Edison General Electric Company, incorporated in New York on April 24, 1889. The company also acquired Sprague Electric Railway & Motor Company that same year.
one_line: Origins of General Electric in 1889, when Thomas Edison's electricity companies were merged into Edison General Electric Company.
key_facts: In 1889, Thomas Edison had business interests in many electricity-related companies.
Edison Lamp Company was a lamp manufacturer in East Newark, New Jersey.
Edison Machine Works was a manufacturer of dynamos and large electric motors in Schenectady, New York.
Bergmann & Company was a manufacturer of electric lighting fixtures, sockets, and other electric lighting devices.
Edison Electric Light Company was the patent-holding company and financial arm backed by J.P. Morgan and the Vanderbilt family for Edison's lighting experiments.
Drexel, Morgan & Co. was a company founded by J.P. Morgan and Anthony J. Drexel.
Drexel, Morgan & Co. financed Edison's research in 1889.
Drexel, Morgan & Co. helped merge Edison's companies under one corporation to form Edison General Electric Company in 1889.
Edison General Electric Company was incorporated in New York on April 24, 1889.
Edison General Electric Company acquired Sprague Electric Railway & Motor Company in 1889.
